# Settings reference

Schema hash `59acd3c6`. Every user-facing setting, as defined in `schema/settings.yaml`; labels and help are the English strings. *Risky* settings arm the timed revert.

## Output

| Id | Label | Values | Default | Tier | Ms | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `output.resolution` ⚠ | Output resolution | Auto, 1080p, 1280x1024, 1280x960, 720p, 480p / 576p, 15 kHz (CRT), Passthrough (exp.), 1024x768 (exp.), 800x600 (exp.), 1600x1200 (exp.), 1920x1200 (exp.) | Auto | essential | M1 | The picture size sent to your display. Auto picks 1280x960 for 60 Hz sources (an exact 4x of 240p) and 1280x1024 for 50 Hz sources. Passthrough sends the source unscaled; HD and PC sources always pass through. Passthrough is experimental: not yet verified on a board. The other (exp.) modes are computed from the display standards; your display must accept them. |
| `output.frameLock` ⚠ | Frame lock | off, on | on | essential | M1 | Makes the output refresh exactly follow the console, which removes judder and tearing. Turn it off only if your display refuses the slightly non-standard rate. |
| `output.force60` ⚠ | Force 60 Hz | off, on | off | advanced | M2 | Outputs 50 Hz (PAL) sources at 60 Hz for displays that do not accept 50 Hz. Frame lock cannot follow a 50 Hz source at 60 Hz, so motion judders slightly (one frame in five is shown twice); leave it off if your display takes 50 Hz. |
| `output.aspect` | Aspect | 4:3, 16:9, Full screen | 4:3 | essential | M2 | The shape of the picture on screen. 4:3 suits most consoles; 16:9 is for games with a widescreen mode; Full screen stretches the picture to the shape of the screen. |
| `output.integerScale` | Integer scale | off, on | off | essential | M2 | Shows every line of the console as the same number of screen lines (four at 1080p for 240p games), so scanlines and pixels come out even. The picture gets a little smaller, with black borders, and Vertical size has no effect while it is on. |
| `output.hPosition` | Horizontal position | -64…64 | 0 | essential | M2 | Moves the picture left or right. |
| `output.vPosition` | Vertical position | -64…64 | 0 | essential | M2 | Moves the picture up or down. |
| `output.hSize` | Horizontal size | -64…64 | 0 | advanced | M2 | Makes the picture narrower or wider. |
| `output.vSize` | Vertical size | -64…64 | 0 | advanced | M2 | Makes the picture shorter or taller. |

## Input

| Id | Label | Values | Default | Tier | Ms | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input.port` | Input | Auto, RGB (SCART/RGBS/VGA), Component (YPbPr) | Auto | essential | M1 | Auto watches all inputs and switches to the one with a signal. RGB covers SCART, the RGBS jacks and VGA; Component is YPbPr. |
| `input.syncThreshold` ⚠ | Sync threshold | -1…31 (-1 = Auto) | -1 | advanced | M2 | The level used to separate sync from sync-on-green or composite sync (it does nothing with separate H/V sync). Auto searches for a stable value; raise it if the picture rolls, lower it if it loses sync on dark scenes. Watch the sync quality while you change it. |
| `input.phase` | Sampling phase | -1…31 (-1 = Auto) | -1 | advanced | M2 | When within each pixel the input is sampled. Adjust while watching fine detail until it is sharp and stable; it matters most for 480p and computer sources. Auto uses the output program's phase. |
| `input.autoGain` | Auto gain | off, on | off | advanced | M1 | While you play, lowers the input gain whenever the brightest parts of the picture clip. It only ever darkens, and starts again for each new source. For exact levels, use Calibrate levels with a white screen instead. |
| `input.videoLpf` ⚠ | Video LPF | Auto, 150 MHz, 110 MHz, 70 MHz, 40 MHz | Auto | advanced | M2 | Filters high frequencies before sampling. Auto chooses per standard; lower values soften the picture and reduce shimmer from noisy sources. |

## Picture

| Id | Label | Values | Default | Tier | Ms | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `picture.brightness` | Brightness | -32…32 | 0 | essential | M1 | Raises or lowers the whole picture. |
| `picture.contrast` | Contrast | -32…32 | 0 | essential | M1 | Increases or decreases the difference between dark and bright areas. |
| `picture.saturation` | Saturation | -32…32 | 0 | essential | M1 | Makes colours stronger or weaker. |
| `picture.sharpness` | Sharpness | Off, Low, Medium, High | Off | essential | M1 | Emphasises edges. Off shows the source as sampled. |
| `picture.scanlines` | Scanlines | off, on | off | essential | M2 | Darkens the gaps between the console's lines to imitate a CRT. Works on 240p and 288p sources and pauses by itself on 480i and 576i. Even lines need an output that is a whole multiple of the source: 960p, 720p or 480p for 240p. |
| `picture.scanlineStrength` | Scanline strength | 1…8 | 4 | essential | M2 | How dark the scanlines are. |
| `picture.deinterlace` | Deinterlacer | Motion adaptive, Bob | Motion adaptive | advanced | M2 | How interlaced pictures are rebuilt. Motion adaptive keeps still detail sharp; Bob has no combing artefacts and the least processing. |

## System

| Id | Label | Values | Default | Tier | Ms | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `system.language` | Language | English, Português (Brasil) | English | essential | M1 | The language of the web page and of the board's screen. On the web page, choose it at the top. The serial console is always English. |
| `system.oledSaver` | Display saver | Off, 1 min, 3 min, 5 min, 10 min | 5 min | advanced | M1 | Turns the display off after a period without use, to protect the OLED from burn-in. |
| `system.encoderReverse` | Reverse knob | off, on | off | advanced | M1 | Swaps the direction of the knob. |
| `system.revertSeconds` | Confirm within | 10 s, 20 s, 30 s | 20 s | advanced | M1 | How long you have to confirm a change that could leave the screen black before it is undone. |
| `system.showAdvanced` | Show advanced | off, on | off | essential | M1 | Shows the settings for sampling, sync and diagnostics, on the web page and in the board's menu. The switch at the bottom of every page is this same setting. |
| `system.startupProfile` | Startup profile | -1…16 (-1 = Last used) (0 = Auto by input) | -1 | essential | M2 | Which profile is in use when the board starts. Last used keeps the one you had, unsaved changes included, unless another console's profile matches the first picture; Auto by input always loads the profile that matches; a number loads that profile. |
